turns.t: G'day. What should I call you, Mr Whitlock or something less formal?
Darren's good. Look, I'm a bit freaked out. There's this ringing in my left ear and it won't stop.
Okay, Darren. How long's it been going?
Three days now. Started on Sunday arvo while I was out in the yard.
Constant, or on and off?
Pretty much constant. It goes quiet when the telly's on, but at night it's really loud.
What does it sound like? A hiss, a buzz, a beep?
More like a high whistle. Like a kettle that never quite boils.
Right. Anything else going on in that ear? Blocked, sore, fluid coming out?
It feels sort of muffled, like I've got cotton wool in there. That's new too.
Muffled on the left only?
Yeah, just the left. The right ear's perfect.
Any spinning or dizziness with it?
No, thank god. I'd have gone straight to emergency. Is this something awful? My neighbour had a tumour thing on his hearing nerve.
That's very uncommon, and it doesn't usually come on over a weekend. Let's have a proper look first.
Okay. Should I be worried about going deaf in that ear?
Let me look before I answer that. Keep still for me.
Left ear canal is partly blocked by a plug of wax. The eardrum behind it looks normal and intact, from what I can see.
Wax? That's it? I've been losing sleep over wax?
Wax can press on the eardrum and cause ringing and that muffled feeling. It's common.
I've never had it before, though. I don't even use cotton buds much.
Even occasionally is enough to pack it in. Best to stop using them altogether.
Right. And do I need drops, or does somebody syringe it out?
We can go over that next visit if it doesn't clear. For now, keep the ear dry in the shower and leave it alone.
How dry? Like a shower cap on my head?
A bit of cotton wool with Vaseline on it in the outer ear is plenty. Don't poke anything in.
Fair enough. My missus swears by those ear candle things, though. She wants me to try one.
Skip them. They don't draw wax out, and I've seen a few nasty burns from them.
I'll tell her the doctor said no. She'll argue, but I'll tell her anyway.
Blame me, that's what I'm here for. Anything else on your mind before we wrap up?
Okay. Before I forget, you probably want to know about allergies. I've got none.
Good, no allergies, thanks for saying so. Pop that in the notes.
And when will the ringing stop? If it's wax, will it be gone straight away?
It should ease over a week or so as the wax shifts. If it's still ringing in two weeks, come back and see me.
And if the hearing drops off completely, or I get dizzy?
Then ring the clinic the same day. Sudden loss in one ear is something we act on quickly.
Got it. Thanks, doc. I'll sleep better tonight.
Good. Cheers, Darren.
